From: Alex Sung <alex.sung@boreashealth.com>

Date: 2027-11-30T07:45:00Z
Subject: Production errors + latency spike in AZ1 - urgent

Team,

We started seeing a big increase in 502/503s and median latency across our inference calls hitting AZ1 at ~07:20 UTC. Error rates are impacting the checkout flow for a small subset of customers and it’s causing user-visible failures (~4% of requests failing, p95 jumping from 180ms to 1.4s). This started right after a traffic spike from a regional marketing campaign.

Can Redwood route our traffic out of AZ1 to the nearest healthy region? We need an immediate mitigation — even a temporary cross-region steer — while you investigate. Please advise ETA and any expected client latency change.

Attached: short packet capture and a few log snippets (we’ll follow up if you need more).

— Alex
Alex Sung

On Tue, Nov 30, 2027 at 07:52 AM kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the head’s up and the pcap. We’re opening an incident and triaging now.

Quick triage summary from infra: we’re seeing repeated TCP retransmits to the AZ1 regional gateway and intermittent LB health flips that are causing amplified retries at our edge. Error pattern lines up with network blips rather than model runtime regressions.

Action plan (initial):
- Initiate cross-region steering for Boreas traffic from AZ1 -> us-west2 (transparent at our API edge)
- Disable aggressive retry policy for the affected prefix to limit amplification
- Apply temporary traffic shaping and a rollback window of 60 minutes to monitor error rate and latency

ETA to start reroute: ~18 minutes. ETA for visible customer improvement: ~5-15 minutes after reroute completes.

Attached: extract of tcpdump and top-line incident logs.

Hannah Schmitt
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-11-30T08:36:00Z
Subject: Re: Production errors + latency spike in AZ1 - urgent

Forwarded message attached for context.

Action update: we completed the transparent steer of Boreas prefix away from AZ1 to us-west2 at 08:33 UTC. Observed client-side p50/p95 for Boreas requests increased by ~22ms / ~87ms respectively (median moved from 180ms -> 202ms, p95 from 1.4s -> 1.487s temporarily) but error rate dropped from ~4% to <0.3% within the first 4 minutes. We also disabled the aggressive retry window which reduced amplification.

Next steps:
- Keep steer active for 6 hours while we monitor (auto rollback if error rate rises)
- Collect full packet traces and control-plane logs, deliver RCA within 72 hours
- Post-mortem will include mitigation runbook (better LB health backoff + regional circuit breakers)

Attachment: reroute-config-v1.diff (diff of edge routing change) and incident log snippet.

Marcus Lin
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Boreas AZ1 incident — executive summary and next steps

Alex / Boreas team —

Thank you for the patience and for sharing diagnostic captures. Final short summary: we observed transient network-level instability in AZ1 that caused LB health flaps and retry amplification resulting in increased 5xxs and latency for your traffic. We implemented a transparent cross-region steer to us-west2 on 2027-11-30T08:33:00Z which brought error rates down to service baseline while adding modest latency.

We’ll keep the steer in place for the next 6 hours to ensure stability, then revalidate AZ1 health before any traffic backfill. Marcus / Hannah will deliver the RCA and detailed mitigation plan within 72 hours.

Commercial note: Rishi has proposed a one-time credit as good will. Rishi — please coordinate with Boreas procurement and finance (cc’d) to confirm amounts and timeline.

Related links: https://drive.redwood.com/incident/boreas-1129, JIRA-INF-9821.

Expect a formal post-incident report; for now, please reach out to me directly if you see any regression.

— Kim
